teams.heading: Former Bulls colleague Chris Rossouw expects Jake White's Fiji to surprise people
teams.body: Jake White's first test in charge is against Japan this Saturday, and former Bulls backline coach Chris Rossouw is already backing him. “I wouldn’t be surprised if they’re going to surprise people,” Rossouw said, adding that he was happy for White. Fiji, ranked 10th and having lost four of five Tests this year, then face France, Ireland and Italy in November.

lead.why: It is the only fresh angle left on the shortlist, framing White's first test in charge against Japan.

teams.heading: Henry Arundell nears Bath return as Muir and de Glanville resume training
teams.body: Head of rugby Johann van Graan said Henry Arundell could be back in the mix this weekend, after the England hopeful missed the start of the season with a back issue. Will Muir and Tom de Glanville have resumed elements of training, but Bath say their availability will be assessed week by week and there is no concrete return date for the trio. One-cap England winger Muir has been out since shoulder surgery last season.

lead.why: It is the freshest England-specific availability news on the shortlist, covering three England hopefuls and a possible return for Henry Arundell.

teams.heading: Robson calls Maxime Lucu's 803 kicking metres 'ridiculous' in 36-36 draw
teams.body: Gloucester scrum-half Dan Robson, an England exile who spent a season with Pau in the Top 14, has called Bordeaux-Bègles' Maxime Lucu's 803 kicking metres 'ridiculous' after the Champions Cup game finished 36-36. Robson said the 'overriding feeling' in the Gloucester huddle was disappointment. Lucu played the night at fly-half, and Robson conceded Gloucester's kick decisions and discipline let Bordeaux into their 22 too often.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item not already run this week, and it puts a France-qualified fly-half's kicking under a rival's spotlight.

teams.heading: Will Greenwood suggests Andy Farrell play Ciaran Frawley at 12
teams.body: Will Greenwood, the 2003 England World Cup winner, says in his view Andy Farrell should solve the No. 10 debate by picking Ciaran Frawley at inside centre alongside Sam Prendergast. Frawley, who quit Leo Cullen's Leinster earlier this year after being overlooked for the 10 shirt, has started impressively at Connacht, and with Jack Crowley unavailable through injury, he is now seen as a genuine rival at 10. Nearly all of his 15 Test caps have come as a replacement.

lead.why: A fresh Ireland selection debate with a clear No. 10 question, and it is a national-squad story rather than the squad announcement already run.

teams.heading: Italy slip to 11th of 12 after three straight Nations Championship defeats
teams.body: Italy are 11th of 12 in the Nations Championship log, with no wins and three defeats from three matches. Across those games they have scored 37 points and conceded 131, a points difference of -94. The latest was a 10-57 loss to Australia in Round 3, and the next assignment is South Africa in Round 4.

teams.heading: Scotland women slump to eighth straight defeat in 56-12 Wallaroos rout
teams.body: Scotland's women lost their eighth straight match on Saturday, beaten 56-12 by Australia in the WXV Global Series in Sydney. Under caretaker head coach Dave Butcher, the Scots led 5-0 early through Katie Buchanan, but the Wallaroos scored five tries before half-time and eight in all. Rachel Malcolm also scored for Scotland. Australia had also beaten Scotland 30-10 in Edinburgh last month.

lead.why: The only shortlist item that is a Scotland story not already run; the men's items have already been covered and the other women's item is the same match.

teams.heading: Macs Page omitted from Wales squad despite four tries this season
teams.body: Scarlets centre Macs Page has been left out of Steve Tandy's 39-man squad for the Nations Championship, despite scoring four tries in four appearances this season. Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies said Page is "probably the first name on the team sheet", and the 21-year-old is qualified for Ireland and has been linked with a Munster offer. Tandy has instead picked Dragons wing Rio Dyer, leaving Page the likely next name in line if injuries strike.

lead.why: A fresh squad omission that matters to Wales, with a live question over whether a qualified-for-Ireland talent could switch allegiance.

teams.heading: Les Kiss admits Wallabies' 22-0 start to Bledisloe II was unacceptable
teams.body: On Saturday in Sydney, Les Kiss was shell-shocked by a first half that gave the All Blacks a 36-7 lead at the break. "None of us accept 22-0," the Wallabies coach said, pointing to line breaks offered and missed tackles. Kiss said several young players had learned a lot, but the team needed to think harder about what it means to turn up. It was back-to-back Bledisloe Cup defeats, with the final score 43-21.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item with Kiss's own reaction to the Sydney defeat, and the Matfield and Wilson/McReight stories have already run.

teams.heading: Hajime Shoji's League One backtracks on foreign-born player rules after backlash
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One backtracked on contentious registration rules on 28 August, after legal challenges and a fierce backlash from players and fans. Naturalised players who acquired Japanese citizenship, or applied for it, by May 2025 will now be treated as Japanese-born under the system due in the 2026-27 season. The original proposal would have kept them outside the Japanese category, cutting places for foreign-born players eligible to represent Japan. Managing Executive Director Hajime Shoji said: "We lacked communication with players who would be adversely affected by the changes."

lead.why: The Japan-eligibility rule reversal is a men's story with real weight for the national pool, and it is not one of the items already run.

teams.heading: Steve Hansen credits Beauden Barrett's midfield marshalling for Sydney Bledisloe win
teams.body: Sir Steve Hansen's view on the Rugby Unity podcast is that Beauden Barrett's work in midfield was a key reason for the Bledisloe Cup win in Sydney: the 35-year-old marshalled Timoci Tavatavanawai and Rieko Ioane, and Hansen says that is something "you can't buy". Barrett started both Bledisloe Tests at full-back, and his form has returned after a difficult Super Rugby Pacific campaign and an underwhelming South Africa tour. New Zealand's 43-21 win on Saturday secured the 2-0 series result.

lead.why: The freshest item on the shortlist, and it is about a player's form, while the Charles gesture story has already run today.

teams.heading: Whiteley confirms Springboks join Sharks ahead of Friday's URC clash with Cardiff
teams.body: Several Springboks have joined the Sharks ahead of Friday night's URC clash with Cardiff at the Arms Park, forwards coach Warren Whiteley confirmed on Tuesday. The group has had just one session together. Whiteley said he was not aware of any injury concerns and that all the players had flown across. He described Cardiff as a quality team and said the set-piece would be a huge battle.

lead.why: It is a fresh, concrete development with Warren Whiteley confirming on the record that Springboks have joined the Sharks, and it has not been reported in previous editions.
